I’ll trace the movement and keyboard-input code, then make the smallest fix and verify it.

Your game already has arrow-key handling, so you shouldn’t need to add the controls from scratch. The likely issue is that the browser is handling the arrow keys too—often by scrolling the page—or that the game isn’t receiving the keypress.

In plain terms, make these changes:

Have the keyboard handler prevent the browser’s default arrow-key action.
Make sure the handler listens for key presses on the whole document, not only when the canvas is focused.
Keep just one movement timer running.

instead of alert what are other methods you could use.

Instead of a browser alert, you could show the message as part of the game:

In-page message: Display "Game Over" and the final score below the canvas. It’s simple and doesn’t interrupt play.
Game-over overlay: Put a message and a Play Again button over the game area. This feels like a natural part of the game.
Toast notification: Show a small message briefly in a corner. It’s less disruptive, but might disappear before the player notices.
Dedicated end screen: Replace the game view with a results screen showing the score and restart options.
